_about: Known firmware bugs, design caveats and reliability problems by drive model. 'match' is a case-insensitive regex on the model name; 'firmware' (optional) lists affected firmware versions — if present the issue applies only to those versions. Extend or override via /data/known_issues.json (same structure; entries are added to these).

issues.title: Firmware bug: rapid health degradation
issues.detail: Firmware 3B2QGXA7 can make the drive's health drop quickly and switch to read-only mode. Back up the data, then update to 5B2QGXA7 or newer with Samsung Magician.

issues.title: Firmware bug: abnormal wear and health drop
issues.detail: Early 990 PRO firmware was reported to burn through the drive's rated endurance unusually fast. Update to 4B2QJXD7 or newer.

issues.title: Firmware bug: drive may become unresponsive
issues.detail: Seagate released SC61 for IronWolf 10TB drives on SC60. The fix addresses drives dropping out of arrays or becoming unresponsive.

issues.title: Firmware bug: 5184-hour failure
issues.detail: Crucial M4 drives on early firmware start hanging after 5,184 power-on hours. Update to 0309 or newer.

issues.title: Spurious pending-sector reports
issues.detail: MX500 firmware can briefly report Current_Pending_Sector = 1 and then clear it. One such blip is usually harmless. Only worry if the count stays up or rises. Newer firmware (M3CR046+) reduces this.

issues.title: SMR drive (WD Red, not Red Plus)
issues.detail: This WD Red uses shingled magnetic recording (SMR). RAID rebuilds and sustained writes can be very slow, and ZFS resilvers may time out. WD Red Plus or Pro (CMR) drives are recommended for NAS arrays.

issues.title: SMR desktop drive in a NAS
issues.detail: This BarraCuda uses shingled magnetic recording (SMR) and isn't designed for RAID. Expect slow rebuilds and timeouts under sustained writes.

issues.title: SMR desktop drive in a NAS
issues.detail: This Toshiba P300/DT02 model uses shingled magnetic recording (SMR). Expect poor RAID rebuild performance.

issues.title: Model with a very high historical failure rate
issues.detail: The Seagate 3TB ST3000DM001 had annual failure rates above 25% in Backblaze's fleet. Plan a replacement even if SMART looks clean.

issues.title: Desktop-class drive
issues.detail: Desktop drives are rated for lighter workloads (~55 TB/yr). They lack RAID error-recovery control (TLER/ERC), so a slow sector can get the whole drive dropped from an array.
